sections.skill: Plan a presentation and tell a text draft from creating a file

questions.prompt: What does a clear presentation structure include?

choices.text: A purpose, main points with evidence, and a close
As many slides as possible, each packed with full paragraphs of text so nothing is left out

questions.correct_answer: A purpose, main points with evidence, and a close
questions.intro: A good PRESENTATION has a clear STRUCTURE: a purpose, a few main points in order, evidence for each, and a closing message, usually with one idea per slide and few words. AI tools can help OUTLINE slides and suggest visuals. Keep two steps apart. (1) A TEXT DRAFT: the tool writes slide titles, bullet points and speaker notes as text. (2) A FILE: an actual slide file must be created in a presentation app or by a tool feature that really makes files. Many chats only produce text, even when they describe "slides." After any file is created or exported, open it and check every slide.

sections.skill: Compare a text draft with a recipe versus a cooked meal

questions.prompt: A text draft of slides is like what?

choices.text: A cooked meal that is ready to serve to guests at the table right now

questions.correct_answer: A recipe
questions.intro: A RECIPE tells you the dishes, ingredients and steps, but you cannot eat it. The MEAL exists only after someone cooks it in a kitchen. A text draft of slides is like a recipe: it lists titles, points and notes. The slide FILE is like the cooked meal: it has to be made in a presentation app or by a feature that really creates files. And just as you taste a meal before serving it, you open and check the file before presenting.

questions.prompt: The slide file is like what?
questions.correct_answer: The cooked meal

sections.title: Apply it

sections.skill: Check exported slides and make the talk your own

questions.prompt: Slides look fine on a laptop but text overflows on the classroom screen. What should have happened?

choices.text: Nothing, since every screen shows slides in exactly the same way regardless of the computer
Checking on the device that will show them

questions.correct_answer: Checking on the device that will show them
questions.intro: Exported slides need checking on the device that will show them: fonts may be replaced, images may be missing, animations may not play, and text may overflow boxes. Generated speaker notes may include claims you cannot support, so check them like any other answer. And a good presentation is yours: reorder, cut and rewrite the draft so it fits your audience and the time you have, often about one slide per minute or two.
